title: Orchestrate JWT compatibility layer and staged OpenSSL backports for SSO adapters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Our SSO surface spans multiple microservices (auth-proxy, console, license-service) that import different JWT and SAML helper libraries. Several services are pinned to older OpenSSL transitive versions which are missing recent CVE backports. Goal: Reduce blast radius by introducing a small runtime compatibility shim for JWT handling, consolidate SSO adapter bindings, and stage targeted OpenSSL backports on the most critical services. This reduces immediate risk while keeping the upgrade window manageable for complex services with heavy binary dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: A single lightweight JWT compatibility adapter (Go + node wrappers) is deployed that normalizes token validation across services
Three high-risk services (auth-proxy, console, license-service) have OpenSSL backports applied and smoke-tested in staging
No behavioral regressions in SSO flows (login, SAML assertions, OIDC refresh) across supported IdPs; validated with automated e2e test harness
Security team signs off on the remediation plan and artifacts (backport patches and compatibility shim)
tasks: Inventory: run dependency-matrix and transitive OpenSSL/JWT/SAML usage scan across repo (list per service)
Prototype: implement Go JWT adapter that wraps both github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go and formcompat for legacy tokens
Backports: prepare minimal OpenSSL 3.0.9 -> 3.0.12 patch set for runtime containers (auth-proxy, console, license-service)
Integration: wire adapter into auth-proxy behind feature flag; add Node shim for console frontend use
Testing: create e2e scenarios for OIDC and SAML logins, assert token validation paths and audit logs
Rollout: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on error budget signals
Documentation: update internal runbooks, developer migration guide, and add confluence page with audit evidence
progress_updates: 2025-02-05: Kicked off inventory; initial scan shows 12 services referencing vulnerable OpenSSL transitive deps; auth-proxy, console, license-service marked high-priority
2025-02-10: Prototype JWT adapter completed (Go); added Node shim using native gRPC call to reduce duplication; basic unit tests added
2025-02-18: Backport patch set drafted and tested locally against staging container image for auth-proxy; observed 0.2% increase in binary size, no perf regression in memoized path
2025-02-24: Security review requested; added preliminary threat model and audit checklist to confluence; asked SecOps to validate patch approach
2025-03-01: Canary deployment started for auth-proxy (5% traffic); no errors in first 24h; plan to expand canary to console next
tradeoffs: Short-term backports minimize risk quickly but prolong the period where we run multiple OpenSSL versions in the fleet. Full upstream upgrades require coordinated rebuilds and may cause longer outages. The compatibility shim adds a small abstraction layer to reduce duplicated validation logic — slight maintenance cost but large reduction in per-service change surface area.
